test.title: The world is running out of sand

paragraphs.text: Sand may seem limitless, but the kind used in construction is becoming scarce. Concrete, glass and roads all require large quantities of it, and global use has roughly tripled in the last twenty years.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Desert sand is plentiful but of little use for building. Its grains have been shaped by wind into smooth, round forms that do not lock together, so concrete made with it is weak. Builders prefer sand from rivers and beaches, whose grains are rougher.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Removing sand from rivers can cause serious damage. It changes the flow of water, increases the risk of flooding downstream and destroys the habitats of fish. In some regions, illegal digging has become so widespread that governments have banned sand mining entirely.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Engineers are looking for alternatives. Crushed rock from quarries can replace river sand in many types of concrete, and some companies grind old glass bottles into a fine powder with similar properties.
paragraphs.label: D
